architectureHistory.title: Formula variable derivation network and focused power-electronics site mode
ownerRequest: Support optional highlighted formula variables inside articles.
A highlighted variable such as D.boost can click through to a detailed derivation page.
Derivation pages should behave like normal editable article pages: Markdown, images, common formatting, and nested links to other derivation variables.
The derivation system should form a maintainable knowledge graph instead of isolated pages.
Data and backups must stay safe.

Short-term public site should feel small and focused: update homepage and power-electronics page only, while hiding digital, analog, circuit-analysis, and project subpages until enough content exists.
architectureDecision: Use a dedicated knowledge/derivation node model instead of overloading ordinary posts or projects.
Reuse existing Markdown renderer, uploads, auth, audit, backup, and CMS patterns wherever possible.
Introduce explicit derivation-link syntax in Markdown, then parse it into clickable highlighted links and optional graph edges.
Keep hidden sections as stored content, not deleted content. Hide navigation and index exposure through site settings.
Do not implement code immediately. Agent00 designs, Agent0 dispatches, child Agents produce API/CMS/frontend/test plans before implementation.
minimalArchitectureChanges: Add public derivation detail page contract.
Add CMS management contract for derivation nodes.
Add site focus mode setting for homepage + power-electronics public scope.
Add backup and regression requirements before release.

architectureHistory.title: Nine implementation-detail architecture decisions and Agent0 implementation-batch design authorization
decision: Dangling derivation links are allowed at authoring time, warn in CMS, and render safely in public without leaking draft or deleted targets.
DOCX V0 degrades to label plus derive slug text, not hyperlink relationships.
The public derivation route is fixed as derive.html?slug=<slug> for V0.
public_focus_mode enters V0 as disabled-by-default site setting.
publishStatus and visibilityStatus are canonical API fields for knowledge nodes.
Hidden landing pages are removed from sitemap and noindexed, but old detail pages are not bulk-noindexed.
rollback.sh should default to gokottamaker before release; until then rollback commands must pass SERVICE_NAME=gokottamaker.
Admin knowledge-node save response is { node, nodes, warnings }.
architectureHistory.agent0Authorization: Agent0 may now design the implementation batch, file boundaries, owner order, and gates. This authorization does not allow child Agents to edit code before Agent0 publishes the batch design and required Git/regression/release gates are satisfied.

maintenancePolicy.updateRule: Update this JSON whenever Agent ownership, output folders, naming rules, release workflow, or project module boundaries change.
beforeWork: Read ACTIVE_AGENT_DISPATCH.json second when it exists; it is the active task entry for all child Agents.
Read TOP_ARCHITECT_HANDOFF.json third for current architecture risks and active roadmap.
If acting as Agent00 or Agent0, run the agentMonitoringProtocol startup scan before making decisions.
Read the target Agent folder's latest handoff or report before editing.
Check git status before staging, deleting, publishing, or moving files.
Run the round update self-check before final response when the task changes modules, contracts, risks, release workflow, or Agent ownership.
Do not overwrite another Agent's active work without explicit owner approval.
maintenancePolicy.rootDirectoryRule: The repository root must stay clean. New reports, test evidence, handoff notes, and temporary explanations must go into the responsible Agent folder, not the root.
rootAllowedHumanDocs: 说明改动情况.md when it is the active release note for the current batch only

roundUpdateSelfCheck.purpose: Every project update must self-check whether permanent docs, Agent interfaces, risks, volume status, release gates, or handoff outputs need updates. The acting Agent must tell the Owner in the conversation when an update is needed, completed, or deferred.
mustRunWhen: Any Agent ownership or interface changes.
Any API, data model, content field, release workflow, or runtime data policy changes.
Any Agent exceeds or approaches its manageable volume threshold.
Any production release, rollback, or Git batch is prepared.
Any permanent project overview or roadmap changes.
checklist: Did the responsible Agent write a handoff/report to its own docs folder?
Did cross-Agent interfaces change and require an AgentX对接AgentY document?
Did risks, blockers, or required Agent00/Agent100 decisions change?
Did Agent volume status change from ok to watch/split-required?
Did release gates or Agent20 regression templates need updates?
Did Agent101 need to audit a new commit batch?
conversationNotificationFormat: 自检结果：已更新 / 待更新 / 无需更新
roundUpdateSelfCheck.handoffFreshnessRule: Each active Agent must keep its latest handoff/report current. If an Agent stops responding or is replaced, the replacement Agent starts by reading PROJECT_MAINTENANCE.json, TOP_ARCHITECT_HANDOFF.json, the latest Agent0 convergence report, and the latest document in the target Agent folder.

agentReportingProtocol.purpose: Make every child-Agent update discoverable by Agent00 and Agent0 without relying on chat history. Reports are append-only in each Agent folder; Agent0/Agent00 monitor by scanning these files plus git status.
reportingRule: Every Agent must write a Markdown report or handoff to its own docs/AgentX folder after meaningful work.
Every Agent must also write a small status JSON beside the report when the work changes files, interfaces, risks, volume status, or release readiness.
Child Agents must not edit the central Agent0 update index directly; Agent0 owns that index to avoid concurrent-write conflicts.
If no code changed but a decision, risk, blocker, or interface changed, the Agent still writes a status JSON.
If an Agent cannot finish, it writes a blocked status JSON before stopping.
minimumMarkdownSections: 需要其他 Agent 配合
阻塞与待 Agent00/Agent100 裁决事项
agentReportingProtocol.failureRule: If an Agent did work but did not produce a status JSON, Agent0 must mark that Agent as reporting-incomplete in the next convergence report and may not treat the work as fully handoff-safe.

agentMonitoringProtocol.purpose: Agent00 and Agent0 must be able to identify recent changes accurately whenever they are executed, regardless of whether they saw the child-Agent chats.
startupScanSteps: List newest files under docs/Agent*/ and docs/Agent*+*/ sorted by timestamp/name.
Read all status JSON files newer than the last Agent0 update index entry.
Read the newest Markdown handoff/report for any Agent whose status JSON is missing, blocked, high risk, split recommended, or reports interface changes.
Compare changedFiles/newFiles/deletedFiles from status JSON with git status.
Check PROJECT_MAINTENANCE.json and TOP_ARCHITECT_HANDOFF.json timestamps and update markers.

If any Agent reports interfacesChanged, risksChanged, split_recommended, split_required, requiresArchitectureDecision, requiresGitAudit, requiresRegression, or requiresReleaseGate, include it in Agent0 convergence.
If status JSON and git status disagree, mark the Agent as needs_audit and request Agent101 or target Agent clarification.
Before final response, tell Owner the monitoring result in conversation.

agentInterfaceContract.purpose: Fixed interfaces for replaceable Agents. Each Agent can be replaced if its latest handoff is current and its inputs, outputs, owned files, and review dependencies are explicit.
globalRules: An Agent owns a domain, not every file it touches.
Cross-domain changes require an AgentX对接AgentY document or Agent0 convergence note.

metrics.ownedFiles: Number of directly owned source/doc/runtime policy files.
metrics.ownedLoc: Approximate lines of directly owned high-change files.
metrics.activeInterfaces: Number of other Agents that must be consulted for normal changes.

metrics.releaseImpact: Whether changes can affect production release or runtime data.

splitThresholds: A single high-change source file owned by the Agent exceeds about 1200 lines and has more than three unrelated workflows.
The Agent must routinely coordinate with more than six other Agents for normal work.
The Agent owns both product semantics and implementation details across unrelated domains.
The Agent repeatedly reports high risk or unresolved architecture decisions.
The latest handoff cannot let a replacement Agent continue safely.
The Agent owns both production release authority and feature implementation authority.
